claim: On a clean GitHub-hosted windows-2022 runner the committed native stores reproduce byte for byte from the pinned XAX compiler, and the native executor really confines the seed artifact there.
label: EXECUTED
scope: one CI runner, the committed sandbox store and the committed seed artifact; the host-granted compiler chain is not part of this run

ci.runner: windows-2022 (GitHub-hosted, clean VM, checkout with core.autocrlf=true)

what_ran: the workflow checked out MrxSiN/XAX at f79b532fd4651ba808676d02f4b038e2cc271e6a and built the server store with python native/server.py

tests/test_native_stdio.py rebuilt native/sandbox.py into xax-mcp-sandbox.exe on that runner and asserted that the produced native/sandbox_request.json and native/xax-mcp-sandbox-gen0.xax are byte for byte the committed files
tests/test_native_stdio.py then ran the built launcher on the committed seed artifact (native/xax-mcp-seed.xax -> 1536-byte PE that calls ExitProcess(40)) and read the 16-byte result record
why_it_matters: The confinement is not a property of this developer machine: a clean Windows Server 2022 image can create the AppContainer profile, hold the process in the job object, and report the artifact's exit code.
The canonical sandbox store and carrier request are machine-independent, so the committed bytes are the authoritative program on every host.

A CRLF-normalizing checkout is proven not to corrupt them: this run also caught that native/sandbox_request.json had been rewritten to CRLF on Windows, which is why .gitattributes now marks every native/*.json as -text.

skipped.reason: CI does not grant XAX_MCP_TEST_COMPILER (the native compiler is a local prototype outside the pinned tree), so the seed -> build -> transaction -> execute chain is exercised only on the development host

limits: This is a pass/fail CI result for one seed artifact, not a security evaluation of the executor.
The runner's OS build, patch level and AppContainer policy differ from the development host; both accepted the container, but only these two hosts were tried.
Linux confinement and the typed I/O contract remain unimplemented; see native-windows-x86_64-sandbox-f79b532.json.
